lead: Salesforce fell about 9.4% with no company news, leading an enterprise-software sell-off (ServiceNow -6.5%, Atlassian -6%, Workday -5.8%, Adobe -4.3%, IGV -3.2%) a day before Anthropic prices its IPO of up to $64.4 billion.
why: Anthropic's IPO (pricing Nov 18, Nasdaq debut Nov 19 as ANT, up to $64.4B raised, ~$1.4T fully diluted valuation) pulled money out of software: outlets say funds are raising cash for it and seat-priced software is the easiest thing to sell; Salesforce fell 17% around SpaceX's June listing too (Yahoo Finance/TIKR).

Renewed fear that AI models and agents automate work across applications, cutting seat counts and pricing power (Seeking Alpha); RBC's Rishi Jaluria said 'the AI companies are going to try to destroy Salesforce entirely'.

Twist: Salesforce owns an Anthropic stake, about 45% of its $11.3B strategic portfolio as of July 31 (Yahoo Finance/TIKR). Wider market also fell (Dow -1.6%, S&P -1%) on tech outages and caution before Nvidia's results. CRM is -18.9% YTD (TipRanks); earnings Dec 2.
